name: Besan Chilla
cuisine: North Indian (Rajasthan, Punjab, Uttar Pradesh; also "besan ka cheela", "besan pudla" in Gujarat, "tomato omelette" in Maharashtra)

ingredients.name: Gram flour (besan)
ingredients.householdMeasure: a scant ½ cup, spooned and levelled

ingredients.name: Onion (pyaz/kanda)
ingredients.householdMeasure: ½ small onion, finely chopped (about ⅓ cup)

ingredients.name: Tomato (tamatar)
ingredients.householdMeasure: ½ small tomato, deseeded and finely chopped (about ¼ cup)

equipment: Flat non-stick tawa or 9-10-inch non-stick pan
Mixing bowl (a deep steel bowl or large mug works)
Measuring spoons and cup (normal teaspoons and a 200 ml steel glass are fine stand-ins)

steps.title: Chop the onion
steps.text: Peel and finely chop 40 g (½ small) onion.
steps.visualCue: Tiny, even pieces about the size of a rice grain, roughly ⅓ cup.
steps.cameraCheck: About ⅓ cup chopped onion on the board
steps.videoShot: The knife rocking through the onion.
steps.watchOut: Big chunks poke through the batter and the chilla tears when you flip; chop them smaller or leave the onion out.

steps.title: Chop the tomato
steps.text: Halve a small tomato, scoop out seeds and juice with a spoon, finely chop 40 g of flesh.
steps.visualCue: Small red cubes with no loose seeds or juice on the board.
steps.videoShot: The spoon scraping out seeds, then dicing.
steps.watchOut: Leaving the seeds in makes the batter watery and the chilla soggy; if the batter turns thin, whisk in 1 tbsp more besan.

steps.title: Chop chilli and coriander
steps.text: Finely chop ½-1 green chilli (3 g) and 1 tbsp (5 g) coriander leaves.
steps.visualCue: Fine green flecks in two small heaps.
steps.cameraCheck: Chilli and coriander side by side
steps.watchOut: Too much chilli makes the whole batch hot; start with ½ chilli, since you cannot take it out later.

steps.title: Grate the ginger
steps.text: Peel and grate ½ tsp (3 g) ginger.
steps.visualCue: A small heap of moist, pale pulp and a sharp, fresh smell.
steps.cameraCheck: ½ tsp grated ginger on a spoon
steps.watchOut: Fibrous strings left in the batter catch on the spatula; pick them out or chop the ginger finer.

steps.title: Measure the besan
steps.text: Spoon 50 g (a scant ½ cup) besan into the bowl and level it.
steps.tip: Spoon the flour into the cup rather than scooping.
steps.visualCue: A small level mound of pale-yellow flour.
steps.watchOut: Scooping with the cup packs in too much flour and the chilla turns thick and doughy; spoon it in instead.

steps.title: Add the dry spices
steps.text: Add ¼ tsp ajwain (crushed between palms), ⅛ tsp turmeric, ¼ tsp Kashmiri chilli powder and ¼ tsp salt. Stir with a spoon.
steps.visualCue: The flour turns evenly light yellow with red and green-brown specks, and smells of thyme from the ajwain.
steps.videoShot: Ajwain rubbed between palms into the bowl.
steps.watchOut: Streaks of plain flour mean uneven salt and colour; stir until the colour is even.

steps.title: Add half the water
steps.text: Pour in about 50 ml (¼ cup) water.
steps.visualCue: A thick, lumpy paste, like soft dough.
steps.watchOut: Pouring all the water at once makes stubborn lumps; keep half back.

steps.title: Whisk out the lumps
steps.text: Whisk the thick paste hard until smooth.
steps.tip: Whisking while the paste is thick breaks lumps much faster than whisking a thin batter.
steps.visualCue: A smooth, thick paste, with no dry pockets when you press the whisk to the side of the bowl.
steps.cameraCheck: The whisk lifted out of the smooth paste
steps.videoShot: The whisk beating in fast circles.
steps.watchOut: Small hard lumps that survive give raw, floury bites; press them against the bowl with a spoon and whisk again.

steps.title: Thin the batter
steps.text: Add the remaining 30-40 ml water a tablespoon at a time, whisking after each, until the batter flows off the spoon in a steady ribbon.
steps.visualCue: Like thin pancake or dosa batter; it coats the back of a spoon and drips off freely.
steps.cameraCheck: Batter falling from a lifted spoon
steps.videoShot: A ribbon of batter falling back into the bowl.
steps.watchOut: Too thick gives a raw, doughy centre; too thin tears when flipped. Fix thick with 1 tbsp water, thin with 1 tbsp besan.

steps.title: Add the vegetables
steps.text: Stir in the onion, tomato, green chilli, ginger and coriander.
steps.visualCue: Flecks of red, white and green spread evenly through the yellow batter.
steps.videoShot: The spoon folding in the vegetables.
steps.watchOut: Tomato releases water, so the batter loosens a little; check it still ribbons off the spoon.

steps.title: Rest the batter (optional)
steps.text: Leave it for 5 min while the tawa heats.
steps.visualCue: The batter thickens slightly as the flour soaks up water.
steps.watchOut: Over-thickened batter spreads badly; whisk in 1 tsp water.

steps.title: Heat the tawa
steps.text: Put the tawa on medium heat. Add ½ tsp oil and spread it with a spoon or folded kitchen paper.
steps.visualCue: A few drops of water flicked on the tawa sizzle and vanish within 2-3 seconds.
steps.watchOut: A tawa that is too cool makes the chilla stick; too hot, and the batter sets before you can spread it. Water that vanishes at once means lower the heat.

steps.title: Pour the first chilla
steps.text: Stir the batter once (vegetables sink). Pour half the batter (about one and a half ladles) into the centre of the tawa.
steps.visualCue: A round puddle of batter with vegetables visible, and a soft sizzle.
steps.watchOut: Skipping the stir gives a chilla of plain batter and a second one full of vegetables.

steps.title: Spread it
steps.text: With the back of the ladle, spread the batter outward in gentle circles to about 7 inches.
steps.visualCue: An even round, a little thicker than a dosa, with no gaps.
steps.watchOut: Pressing hard tears the batter and it sticks to the ladle; if it drags, lower the heat and spread lighter and quicker.

steps.title: Drizzle oil
steps.text: Drizzle ½ tsp oil around the edge and a few drops on top.
steps.visualCue: The oil sizzles at the edges.
steps.watchOut: Pools of oil on top make it greasy; use only a few drops.

steps.title: Cook the first side
steps.text: Leave it on medium heat, untouched.
steps.visualCue: The top changes from wet and glossy to dull and dry-looking; the edges lift and turn golden.
steps.cameraCheck: A spatula lifting the edge to show a golden underside
steps.videoShot: The top going from shiny to matte.
steps.watchOut: Flipping while the top is still shiny breaks the chilla. Wait until the edges lift on their own and the spatula slides under easily.

steps.title: Flip it
steps.text: Slide the spatula fully under the chilla and flip in one quick move.
steps.visualCue: A golden-brown underside with darker spots where the onion touched the tawa.
steps.cameraCheck: The flipped chilla showing the golden side
steps.watchOut: A slow, half-under flip folds or tears it; slide the spatula in all the way, and if it tears, press the pieces together and carry on.

steps.title: Cook the second side
steps.text: Press lightly with the spatula and cook.
steps.visualCue: Brown spots on the second side; the centre feels firm, not soft, when pressed.
steps.cameraCheck: The second side lifted on the spatula
steps.watchOut: A soft, pale centre means it is still raw inside and tastes of raw flour; give it another 30 sec on low heat.

steps.title: Plate the first chilla
steps.text: Fold it in half or slide it flat onto a plate.
steps.visualCue: Golden, slightly crisp edges and a soft centre, with no wet patches.
steps.cameraCheck: The first chilla on the plate
steps.videoShot: The chilla sliding onto the plate.
steps.watchOut: Stacking hot chillas without a gap makes them steam and go limp; fold or lay them side by side.

steps.title: Re-oil the tawa
steps.text: Lower the heat for a moment, add ½ tsp oil and spread it.
steps.tip: Letting the tawa cool slightly before the second pour helps the batter spread instead of setting in lumps.
steps.visualCue: A thin, even film of oil.
steps.watchOut: Skipping this step makes the second chilla stick to the tawa.

steps.title: Make the second chilla
steps.text: Turn the heat back to medium. Stir the remaining batter, then repeat steps 13-19 (pour, spread, drizzle ½ tsp oil, cook 2-2.5 min, flip, cook 1.5-2 min).
steps.visualCue: Same as the first: golden, set, no raw centre.
steps.watchOut: Leftover batter that has thickened spreads badly; whisk in 1 tsp water first.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Serve hot, folded or stacked, with green chutney or ketchup on the side.
steps.visualCue: Two golden rounds dotted with red, white and green.
steps.videoShot: A slow pan across the plate as a piece is torn off.
steps.watchOut: Chillas go limp within minutes of cooling; eat straight away.

reasons: besan gives about 11 g of plant protein and 5 g of fibre in 50 g, with a lower glycaemic load than refined-flour breakfasts, and the dish is shallow-cooked in only 2 tsp oil with onion, tomato and herbs. It is naturally gluten-free and vegan. Points come off for the small vegetable amount, modest protein for a full meal, and about 625 mg sodium. Restaurant and street versions are often buttered or made with extra oil and served with sweet ketchup or mayonnaise dips.

researchRating.basis: a hugely popular everyday North Indian breakfast, widely featured as a quick, high-protein, vegan "eggless omelette". Recipe pages seen in search results this cycle: Hebbar's Kitchen 5/5 from 268 votes; Vegrecipesofindia about 4.59/5 from 31 votes on the print page (a third-party aggregator showed 4.8 from 65 ratings); Cook With Manali 5/5 from 3 votes; WhiskAffair 4.2 from 12 ratings (small samples). Small deductions because it is seen as a plain everyday dish, and because people often report chillas sticking, breaking or tasting raw if the batter or heat is wrong (WhiskAffair and Eat Healthy 365 both address sticking).

storage: Best eaten fresh; chillas go limp as they cool. Cooked chillas keep in an airtight box in the fridge for up to 1 day (butter paper between them). Freezing is not recommended; they turn rubbery. Reheat on a hot dry tawa for about 30-40 sec per side. Uncooked batter without tomato keeps in the fridge for 1 day; add the tomato just before cooking.
leftoverRemix: Chilla kathi roll. Warm a leftover chilla on the tawa, spread 1 tsp green chutney, add strips of onion and cucumber and 2 tbsp crumbled paneer or leftover sabzi, sprinkle chaat masala, roll tightly and wrap the bottom half in butter paper.
burnOff: about 4.4 km of running (305 ÷ 70 kcal/km, 70 kg adult), or about 6.1 km of brisk walking (about 1 hr 15 min at 5 km/h, using about 50 kcal/km) (est.).

navratri.reason: besan (chickpea flour) and onion are not eaten in most vrat rule sets (assumed: no grains or pulses, no onion)

ekadashi.reason: besan is a pulse flour, and pulses and grains are avoided on Ekadashi in the common rule set

jain.reason: skip onion and fresh ginger, use sonth (dry ginger powder)

ramadan.reason: meat-free, 12 g protein and 7 g fibre keep you full for sehri; moderate sodium (about 625 mg), so use less salt at sehri

jain.reason: drop the onion and fresh ginger (root vegetables) and use a pinch of dry ginger powder (sonth) instead; tomato, green chilli and coriander are fine

vegan.reason: besan, vegetables, spices and oil only; no dairy, ghee or honey

sattvik.reason: leave out the onion and add extra chopped tomato or capsicum (recipe has no garlic)

glutenFree.reason: besan is chickpea flour; the recipe uses no hing (most hing sold in India is compounded with wheat flour, so skip it or buy gluten-free hing)

dairyFree.reason: no dairy in the chilla; serve with a curd-free chutney

variants.reason: . Main recipe is gluten-free (leave out hing, or use gluten-free hing).
